pages: Precedent memo: Tarrow Freight v. Delling
Multnomah County Circuit Court, trial ruling 2024-03-11 - memo by the employment group

The court refused to enforce a 24-month non-compete against a freight dispatcher because the employer never gave written notice of the non-compete two weeks before the start date, as ORS 653.295 requires.
Delling accepted an offer by email on 2022-12-27 and started on 2023-01-16. The offer email mentioned the non-compete; the signed agreement arrived on the first day.
We represented Delling and argued the notice defect alone. Lesson: ask the client for the dated offer letter first.
Had the court reached scope, the 24-month term and the three-state radius would likely have been narrowed to 12 months.
Tarrow claimed 180,000 dollars in lost contracts. The court did not reach damages.
Keep the dated documents from the first client call. The dates usually decide these cases.

Reversed on appeal (Oregon Court of Appeals, A181442). The appellate court held that the offer email of 2022-12-27, 20 days before the start date, was written notice. Section 1 above is no longer good law and must not be cited.

memos.holding: The court enforced a 12-month non-compete against a hygienist. Written notice was given in the offer letter 19 days before the start date, which satisfied ORS 653.295.
memos.facts: Soto signed the offer letter on 2021-04-02 and started on 2021-04-21. She opened a competing practice 6 miles away in 2022-01.
memos.position: We represented Brightwater. The offer letter date decided notice; scope was reasonable at 12 months and 10 miles.

memos.holding: The non-compete was void because Amundsen's salary was below the statutory threshold for the year he was hired.
memos.facts: Amundsen earned 61,300 dollars as a routing analyst. The threshold that year was 100,533 dollars.
memos.position: We represented Amundsen. Check the salary threshold for the hire year before anything else.

memos.holding: A 24-month non-compete for a sales director was cut to 12 months. Terms longer than 12 months are presumptively unreasonable for non-executive staff.
memos.facts: Petrov ran regional sales for a lumber mill and left for a competitor in Idaho.
memos.position: We represented Harlan. Expect any term over 12 months to be narrowed.

memos.holding: A non-solicitation clause was enforced even though the non-compete in the same agreement failed; the court severed the two.
memos.facts: Nakamura, a physical therapist, emailed 40 former patients in her first week at the new clinic.
memos.position: We represented Quarry Point. Plead non-solicitation separately from the non-compete.

memos.holding: A non-compete signed at a promotion, not at hire, was unenforceable unless it was entered into upon a bona fide advancement and the employee received notice two weeks before the promotion took effect.
memos.facts: Ahmed was promoted to engineering manager on 2022-06-01 and handed the agreement the same morning.
memos.position: We represented Ahmed. Promotion agreements need the same two-week notice.

memos.holding: The court refused to enforce the non-compete because the employer never sent Ruiz a signed copy of the agreement within 30 days after his employment ended.
memos.facts: Ruiz managed the propagation greenhouse and left on 2022-05-31. The signed copy was first sent with the complaint in 2022-09.
memos.position: We represented Ruiz. Ask when, if ever, the signed copy was sent after termination.

memos.holding: The non-compete was void because Moreno was paid by the hour and was not exempt from overtime; the statute reaches only salaried, exempt employees.
memos.facts: Moreno was a head brewer paid 31 dollars an hour with overtime.
memos.position: We represented Moreno. Hourly pay ends the analysis.

memos.holding: A non-compete for an employee below the salary threshold was enforced only because the employer paid her half of her salary for the whole restricted period.
memos.facts: Kask was an escrow officer; Juniper paid 50 percent of her salary for the 6-month restriction.
memos.position: We represented Kask and lost. Garden-leave pay can save an otherwise void non-compete.

memos.holding: Final paycheck penalty wages were awarded because the last check was issued 6 business days after termination, not by the end of the next business day.
memos.facts: Flynn was fired on a Tuesday; the check was mailed the next Wednesday.
memos.position: We represented Flynn. Penalty wages run up to 30 days.

memos.holding: Meal-break claims failed because the employer's records showed 30-minute breaks and the crew lead's testimony was not specific.
memos.facts: Reyes claimed 2 years of missed meal breaks on roofing crews.
memos.position: We represented Summit. Time records beat general testimony.

memos.holding: A nurse's retaliation claim survived summary judgment because the schedule cut followed her safety complaint by 9 days.
memos.facts: Castillo filed a staffing complaint on 2023-02-01; her shifts were cut from 4 to 2 a week on 2023-02-10.
memos.position: We represented Castillo. Timing alone carried summary judgment.

memos.holding: Overtime was owed for pre-shift safety meetings of 15 minutes that the employer treated as unpaid.
memos.facts: Bao attended daily 6:45 am safety briefings before a 7:00 am shift for 18 months.
memos.position: We represented Bao. Mandatory meetings are work time.

memos.holding: A tip-pooling arrangement that included managers was unlawful and the tips were ordered repaid.
memos.facts: Grant was a server; shift managers took a share of the pool for 2 years.
memos.position: We represented Grant. Managers may not share in tip pools.

memos.holding: A commission dispute was decided on the written commission plan, not the broker's verbal promise.
memos.facts: Oduya claimed a verbal 4 percent split; the written plan said 3 percent.
memos.position: We represented Pinecrest. Get the written plan first.

memos.holding: A 9-month non-compete for an orthodontic office manager was enforced; notice was given in a written offer 16 days before her start date.
memos.facts: Lindqvist received the offer letter on 2023-08-14 and started on 2023-08-30.
memos.position: We represented Cascade Ortho. A written offer that names the non-compete is notice.

citator.text: Citator note, 2025-06-02: Tarrow Freight v. Delling (Multnomah County Circuit Court, 2024) was REVERSED by the Oregon Court of Appeals (A181442). The offer email counted as written notice. Do not cite the trial ruling on notice.
Citator note, 2023-03-30: Brightwater Dental v. Soto (Lane County Circuit Court, 2022) was affirmed without opinion. Good law.
Citator note, 2023-09-12: Kestrel Logistics v. Amundsen (Washington County Circuit Court, 2023) - no appeal filed. Good law.
Citator note, 2024-02-11: Harlan Mills v. Petrov (Oregon Court of Appeals, 2023) - review denied by the Oregon Supreme Court. Good law.
Citator note, 2025-01-08: Quarry Point Clinic v. Nakamura (Deschutes County Circuit Court, 2024) - settled on appeal, the judgment stands. Good law.
Citator note, 2024-08-19: Corvid Software v. Ahmed (Oregon Court of Appeals, 2024) - review denied. Good law.
Citator note, 2023-06-01: Alder Grove Nursery v. Ruiz (Marion County Circuit Court, 2023) - no appeal filed. Good law.
Citator note, 2022-10-04: Basalt Brewing v. Moreno (Deschutes County Circuit Court, 2022) - no appeal filed. Good law.
Citator note, 2024-09-30: Juniper Title v. Kask (Clackamas County Circuit Court, 2024) - appeal dismissed. Good law.
Citator note, 2025-04-22: Cascade Ortho v. Lindqvist (Multnomah County Circuit Court, 2025) - no appeal filed. Good law.

questions.say: A new client says their employer never gave written notice of the non-compete two weeks before they started. Is the non-compete unenforceable in Oregon? Cite the precedent we have.
What is our best precedent for voiding a non-compete when the signed agreement only came on the first day of work?
Our client got the non-compete only on her first day, although the offer email mentioned it. Can we get it thrown out for lack of notice? Which of our cases supports that?
